title: Microsoft Defender and Sentinel SIEM
description: Explore Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel to understand Azure's security posture management and SIEM capabilities.

data.text: Azure provides two powerful services for security monitoring. **Microsoft Defender for Cloud** continuously assesses your security posture and finds weaknesses. **Microsoft Sentinel** is a cloud-native SIEM that collects logs, detects threats, and helps you respond to incidents.

data.title: What Defender for Cloud does
items: **Secure score** — Rates your overall security posture from 0 to 100% with actionable recommendations.
**Threat protection** — Built-in alerts for Azure services (VMs, storage, SQL, App Service) without extra agents.
**Regulatory compliance** — Maps your environment to standards like PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, and SOC 2.
**Agentless scanning** — For VMs, Defender collects data through the Azure fabric rather than installing software.

data.text: A SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system collects log data from every corner of your environment, correlates events, and surfaces real threats. Sentinel is Microsoft's cloud-native SIEM built directly on Azure.

data.title: Defender for Cloud vs. Microsoft Sentinel

cards.title: Defender for Cloud
cards.description: Continuous security posture assessment and threat protection for your Azure (and hybrid) resources.
pros: No extra cost for basic secure score
cons: Primarily focused on posture, not deep log analytics

cards.title: Microsoft Sentinel
cards.description: Cloud-native SIEM and SOAR platform that ingests logs from any source and correlates them to find threats.
pros: Ingests data from any source (Azure, AWS, on-prem)

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Defender for Cloud monitors your resource configuration and raises alerts on threats
Sentinel collects and correlates logs across Azure, AWS, and on-premises environments
The two services work best together — Defender feeds Sentinel for deeper investigation
Start with Defender's free tier, then add Sentinel when you need SIEM capabilities
data.takeaway: Think of Defender for Cloud as your daily security check-up and Sentinel as your 24/7 security operations center.
